propositions: A disposition-closed child (duplicate, not_a_bug, escalated) with a live replacement link is unsigned by design in the close path but required to carry a completion-verifier attestation in the certification path, creating an uncertified state with no honest remedy.

The close path exempts dispositions from completion verification at transition_close.py:253-260, minting no attestation; the certification path ignores this exemption and demands valid completion-verifier on every closed direct child, withholding the parent's signature.

An honestly-declared duplicate cannot be certified through any non-force path: deleting the replacement link is the only escape, forcing a choice between documenting the replacement relationship honestly or obtaining a signature.

A disposition close must mint a completion-verifier attestation with manifest reading 'DISPOSITION <class>' rather than claiming a 'PASS', so the exemption is transparent in the audit record and validity-on-read remains intact.
The --force-close guard must run before the disposition branch to prevent forced closes from becoming a bypass of verification requirements.
